rows.selection_reason: No prior evidence exists, so the first experiment should establish a simple, interpretable baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal RNA configuration: a standard linear dimensionality reduction on a single profile with no aggregation or fusion complexity. This gives a clear floor for RNA-only performance. It is the best use of experiment 1 because (1) it isolates the RNA modality with the least confounding design choices, (2) it provides a reference point against which I can compare image-only (config_010) in experiment 2 to determine which modality carries the strongest signal, and (3) it avoids prematurely committing budget to complex multimodal or multiprofile settings before knowing whether a simple single-modality model is already competitive. Establishing this baseline first lets the remaining 9 experiments be allocated strategically toward the most promising direction.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved only ~48.5% validation accuracy, a weak baseline that gives little signal about which design axis (modality, encoder, aggregation, fusion) will drive improvement. Uncertainty: The most critical open question is whether the image modality carries substantially more discriminative information than the RNA profile for this task. This experiment tests image_only with a strong pretrained encoder (resnet50) at the same singleprofile setting, providing a clean modality-level comparison against config_001. If image_only substantially outperforms 48.5%, it strongly justifies investing remaining budget in multimodal configurations; if it is comparable or worse, it signals that the bottleneck is representation quality (encoder choice) rather than modality, redirecting effort toward scvi/scgpt encoders. This is the highest-information single experiment at this stage because the modality decision gates the architecture of all subsequent multimodal experiments (configs 016-051) and determines where to focus the remaining 8 experiments.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is very weak at 20.8%, indicating RNA is the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether the PCA representation is already near-optimal for RNA or whether a learned encoder (scVI) can extract more discriminative signal. This experiment (config_004: rna_only, singleprofile, scvi_n200) isolates the RNA encoder choice as the single variable changed from config_001, directly testing if a learned, biologically-informed representation outperforms linear PCA. If scVI improves accuracy, it justifies investing further experiments in learned encoders and potentially multimodal fusion with a stronger RNA backbone. If it does not, PCA is sufficient and we can pivot to exploring multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion. With 7 experiments remaining, establishing the best RNA representation early is critical because it underpins all multimodal configurations.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (0.5203 acc, config_004), outperforming pca_n2000 (0.4849, config_001), while image-only is very weak (0.2079). The multiprofile axis is entirely untested. Question: Does multiprofile with avgpool aggregation improve over singleprofile using the same scvi_n200 encoder? This isolates the effect of multiprofile+aggregation (the only change from config_004) while holding the RNA encoder fixed. Why this is best: With 6 experiments remaining, establishing whether multiprofile helps at all is the highest-priority design question before investing in more complex multimodal or transformer-aggregation variants. If multiprofile+avgpool does not beat 0.5203, it would redirect budget toward encoder exploration (scgpt) or multimodal fusion; if it does, it justifies testing transformer aggregation and multimodal extensions next.

The current best result is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.6501 accuracy, showing a large gain over single-profile (0.5203). The key open question is whether transformer aggregation can outperform avgpool for multiprofile RNA representations. Config_006 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping scvi_n200 and multiprofile fixed, providing a clean isolation of the aggregation effect. This is the best use of experiment 5 because: (1) it directly exploits the strongest evidence (multiprofile + scvi_n200), (2) it tests a single variable to reduce uncertainty about aggregation, and (3) the answer will inform the aggregation choice for all remaining multimodal experiments (configs 018-051), making it a high-leverage decision under the 5-experiment remaining budget.

The current best (config_006: scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, acc 0.653) shows that multiprofile + scvi_n200 is the dominant configuration, with a ~13% jump over singleprofile. The encoder choice matters (scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 at singleprofile: 0.52 vs 0.48), but scgpt has not been tested at all. Config_009 (scgpt, multiprofile, transformer) directly isolates the RNA encoder variable against the current best (config_006), testing whether a pretrained generative encoder (scgpt) can outperform scvi_n200 at the multiprofile level. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve before committing remaining budget to multimodal fusion experiments, because the RNA encoder choice will propagate into all multimodal configurations. If scgpt wins, we shift to scgpt-based multimodal configs; if scvi_n200 holds, we confirm the encoder and pivot to multimodal exploration with 4 experiments left.

The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy. The key open question is whether adding the image modality can improve upon this strong RNA-only baseline. Image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.208), suggesting limited standalone value, but it may still provide complementary signal in a fused setting. Config_032 directly extends config_006 by adding resnet50 image features with the same transformer aggregation and a simple concat fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion on top of the best-known RNA configuration. This is the cleanest single-variable extension of our best result. If it fails to beat 0.653, we can confidently conclude RNA-only multiprofile is optimal and use remaining budget to confirm; if it helps, we can explore weighted fusion or ViT-L in the remaining 3 experiments.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc. The image-only resnet50 baseline was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image modality's contribution in the multimodal model may be limited by the encoder quality. Config_038 isolates the image encoder effect by replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings identical to the best config (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, concat). This is a single-variable change from the current best, making it a clean test. If ViT-L substantially improves the image component, it could yield a meaningful accuracy gain and open a productive direction for the remaining 2 experiments (e.g., testing weighted fusion with ViT-L). If it does not, it confirms the image modality is inherently limited here, redirecting effort toward RNA-side refinements. This high-information experiment is the best use of slot 8 given the uncertainty about whether a stronger image encoder can unlock more multimodal benefit.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.7207 accuracy. The only untested single-variable modification of this best config is the fusion strategy: weighted vs. concat. All other dimensions (RNA encoder=scvi_n200, profile=multiprofile, image=imagenet_vit_l, aggregation=transformer) are well-supported by prior evidence as the optimal choices. Config_039 isolates the effect of weighted fusion in the strongest known setup. With only one experiment remaining after this, exploiting the best direction with a minimal, well-motivated change maximizes the probability of either finding a new best or confirming the current best is near-optimal, rather than exploring a less-supported branch.

The current best is config_039 (0.725 acc, multimodal/multiprofile/scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/weighted). Evidence shows scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, and weighted fusion are the strongest choices, with transformer aggregation only marginally ahead of avgpool in RNA-only (0.653 vs 0.650). Since this is the final experiment, the goal is to exploit the best-identified direction. config_037 changes only the aggregation from transformer to avgpool while retaining weighted fusion and all other best components, isolating whether simple averaging of profiles might interact differently with the strong image modality (ViT-L) than attention-based aggregation. This single-variable test from the current best is the highest-probability route to a marginal improvement or confirmation, and avoids the risk of introducing a weaker component (e.g., scgpt or resnet50) that would almost certainly underperform.
